legend: Gastric body resection shows a small neuroendocrine (micro)tumor arising in gastric oxyntic mucosa with prominent proton pump inhibit effect and multifocal nodular enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia in the deep mucosa.

Gastric body resection shows multiple small neuroendocrine tumors arising in a background atrophic gastritis characterized by chronic gastritis, loss of parietal cells, intestinal metaplasia and enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia.

Gastric body resection shows multiple small polypoid gastric neuroendocrine tumors arising in the oxyntic mucosa with prominent hypertrophic changes: numerous dilated oxyntic glands filled with inspissated material, parietal cell hyperplasia and enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia/dysplasia.

diagnosis: Gastric neuroendocrine carcinoma, small cell type
legend: Gastric resection shows a large ulcerated mass composed of sheets of neoplastic cells with scant cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei without nucleoli. There are tumor necrosis, numerous mitoses and apoptosis. Note that background stomach with chronic gastritis and intestinal metaplasia.

Gastric body resection shows a large, ulcerated neuroendocrine tumor invading muscularis propria with normal background gastric oxyntic mucosa. Note gastric mucosa overlying or immediate to the tumor can show loss of parietal cells and intestinal metaplasia, mimicking atrophic gastritis.

diagnosis: Gastric neuroendocrine carcinoma, small cell type
legend: Gastric resection shows a large ulcerated mass composed of sheets of neoplastic cells with scant cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei without nucleoli. There are tumor necrosis, numerous mitoses and apoptosis. Note that background stomach with chronic gastritis and intestinal metaplasia.
Neoplastic cells arranged in small clusters, ribbons and cords extending beyond the muscularis mucosae.
A The endoscopic appearance is characterized by multiple, small, polypoid lesions in the gastric body or fundus.
A The endoscopic appearance is characterized by single or multiple, small, polypoid lesion in the gastric body or fundus.
B Tumour cells are arranged in nests and clusters with background gastric mucosa shows parietal cell hyperplasia and oxyntic gland dilation.
A The tumour is arising in the antrum with background chronic gastritis.
C The neoplastic cells display diffuse synaptophysin staining.
B Solid sheets of small cells with hyperchromatic nuclei lacking nucleoli, frequent mitoses, abundant apoptotic bodies, and tumour necrosis.
A well-differentiated NET with typically normal background gastric mucosa and no parietal cell hyperplasia.
A There are two distinct morphologies: adenocarcinoma with glandular formation (well differentiated in this case) and NET.
B The neuroendocrine component is positive for synaptophysin.
B A small polypoid lesion arising in a background of atrophic gastritis.
C In a high-power field, gastric NET shows cords/nests of well-differentiated NET cells intermixed with benign gastric glands.
D The background atrophic gastritis shows nodular/linear enterochromaffin-like–cell hyperplasia as highlighted by synaptophysin immunohistochemistry.
A The tumour has poorly differentiated morphology, composed of cells with moderate to abundant cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, or nuclei with prominent nucleoli.
B Diffuse synaptophysin labelling.
C High Ki-67 proliferative index (75%).
